```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

XCNV annotates copy-number variants (CNVs) and scores them in two separate
lanes:

- **X-CNV**: the published X-CNV model (Zhang et al. 2021) gives each CNV an
  `MVP_score`, a model probability of pathogenicity. It is not a clinical class.
- **ACMG/ClinGen**: the 2019 constitutional CNV standard. Each criterion is one
  evidence row that you can inspect, change and rescore.

DuckDB does the overlap joins. R does validation, feature reduction, the tree
evaluator and scoring. No bedtools and no XGBoost are needed at run time.
Ownership, output contracts and validation rules are in
[`ARCHITECTURE.md`](ARCHITECTURE.md).

## Installation

```r
install.packages(
  "XCNV",
  repos = c("https://rgenomicsetl.r-universe.dev", "https://cloud.r-project.org")
)
```

## Example: a ClinVar deletion

The package includes the annotations for one real case, ClinVar allele 72461:
a pathogenic deletion that contains `SOX2`.

```{r real-case}
library(XCNV)
example <- xcnv_real_example()
example$clinvar[, c("clinvar_allele_id", "clinical_significance",
                    "grch37_chrom", "grch37_start0", "grch37_end0")]
```

### X-CNV score

```{r real-prediction}
prediction <- predict_cnv(example$cnv, example$resources)
prediction[, c("Chr", "Start", "End", "Type", "gain.freq", "loss.freq",
               "pLI", "Episcore", "GHIS", "MVP_score")]
```

### ACMG/ClinGen evidence and class

The deletion contains `SOX2`, an established haploinsufficient gene, so
criterion 2A gives one point.

```{r real-evidence}
cnv <- transform(example$cnv, cnv_id = example$clinvar$cnv_id,
                 cnv_type = type, assembly = "GRCh37")
genes <- transform(example$genes, assembly = "GRCh37")
dosage <- transform(example$dosage, assembly = "GRCh37")
evidence <- derive_cnv_2019_evidence(cnv, genes, dosage)
evidence[, c("criterion", "score", "source_id", "evidence_id")]
score_cnv_2019(evidence)[, c("cnv_id", "cnv_type", "score", "classification", "status")]
```

The automatic provider derives sections 1 and 3 and the section 2 criteria
of established dosage-sensitive and benign records from gene and dosage
tables ([sections 1 and 2](#sections-1-and-2)), and criterion 4O from a
population CNV table when you give one ([criterion 4O](#criterion-4o)).
Phenotype, inheritance, segregation, case and partial-gene evidence are extra
rows that you supply.

## GRCh38 calls

The X-CNV model and its resources are GRCh37. Declare a liftover to score
GRCh38 calls. XCNV lifts each call with DuckHTS and scores the GRCh37 interval:

```r
liftover <- xcnv_liftover(
  chain = "xcnv-resources/liftover/GRCh38_to_GRCh37.chain.gz",
  source_fasta = "GRCh38.fa", destination_fasta = "GRCh37.fa",
  source_assembly = "GRCh38", destination_assembly = "GRCh37",
  release = "ensembl-76-GRCh38_to_GRCh37"
)
predict_cnv(grch38_calls, resources, liftover = liftover)
```

The chain is Ensembl's GRCh38 to GRCh37 assembly mapping, which Ensembl
publishes without restriction on use. DuckHTS reads it compressed and matches
contigs with or without `chr`, so it lifts calls on a `chr1`-named GRCh38 FASTA
to a `1`-named GRCh37 FASTA as published.

The chain also maps GRCh38 regions to GRCh37 patch contigs (`HG1423_PATCH` and
others), which a primary GRCh37 FASTA such as `human_g1k_v37` lacks. DuckHTS
follows the chain and does not check the destination contig against the
destination FASTA. A call with an end in such a region is `unsupported`, with
`contig_changed` or `end_unmapped`. On 3,735 ClinVar copy-number records with
both GRCh38 and GRCh37 coordinates, lifted from the GIAB GRCh38 FASTA to
`human_g1k_v37`, the chain lifts 3,458 calls (92.6%); the same chain without
its patch-contig chains lifts 3,568 (95.5%) and changes no lifted interval.

Each row keeps its GRCh38 coordinates and adds the lifted interval. A call that
does not lift to one interval on the same contig and strand is `unsupported`,
with a `liftover_reason` and no `MVP_score`. The ACMG/ClinGen lane works on
GRCh38 directly.

## Resources

The resources are on Hugging Face at
[`RgenomicsETL/xcnv-resources`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/RgenomicsETL/xcnv-resources).
`SHA256SUMS` covers every file.

| Folder | Contents | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `grch37/` | X-CNV annotations and model | X-CNV lane |
| `grch38/` | GENCODE 50 genes and ClinGen dosage as Parquet, with `sources.tsv` | ACMG/ClinGen lane |
| `liftover/` | Ensembl GRCh38 to GRCh37 chain | X-CNV lane on GRCh38 calls |

Score calls with the X-CNV lane:

```r
resources <- xcnv_resources("xcnv-resources/grch37", require = "annotations")
predictions <- predict_cnv(read_cnv("input.bed"), resources)
write_xcnv(predictions, "predictions.output.csv")
```

`xcnv_resource_manifest()` lists the required files. `run_xcnv()` does the
same in one call.

Derive ACMG/ClinGen evidence for GRCh38 calls:

```r
con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb())
genes <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "FROM 'xcnv-resources/grch38/genes.parquet'")
dosage <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "FROM 'xcnv-resources/grch38/dosage.parquet'")
calls <- data.frame(
  cnv_id = "sox2-del", chr = "chr3", start = 181700000, end = 181800000,
  cnv_type = "loss", assembly = "GRCh38"
)
evidence <- derive_cnv_2019_evidence(calls, genes, dosage)
score_cnv_2019(evidence)
```

On these relations the call above scores 1 point (2A, `SOX2`): pathogenic.

`tools/build_grch38_resources.R` rebuilds `grch38/` from SHA-256-pinned
sources. `tools/build_grch38_population.R` builds the population relation of
criterion 4O, `grch38/population.parquet`, from the gnomAD-SV 4.1 sites file
(CC0 1.0), pinned by SHA-256.

### Sections 1 and 2

`derive_cnv_2019_evidence()` reads the ClinGen dosage relation for section 1
and section 2 (Riggs et al. 2020, Tables 1 and 2, and Supplemental Material
1). A record is established at score 3 and benign at score 40 ("dosage
sensitivity unlikely"). A loss reads the haploinsufficiency score, a gain the
triplosensitivity score. The functional genes (`functional_biotypes`,
protein-coding by default) stand for the standard's protein-coding genes.

| Criterion | Points | Rule | Source |
|---|---:|---|---|
| 1A | 0 | The CNV overlaps a functional gene, or an established record of either score (`dosage:<ids>`), such as the non-coding *TERC* or *XIST* gene | 1A: "protein-coding or other known functionally important elements" |
| 1B | -0.60 | Neither | 1B |
| 2A | 1 | The CNV contains an established record | 2A |
| Loss 2F | -1 | A benign record contains the loss | Table 1, 2F: "completely contained within an established benign CNV region" |
| Loss 2G | 0 | The loss overlaps benign records, none contains it | Table 1, 2G |
| Gain 2C | -1 | The gain has the record's interval, or crosses one record boundary and holds the record's genes, at least one, with no breakpoint in a gene | Table 2, 2C: "identical in gene content" |
| Gain 2D | -1 | The record contains the gain, no breakpoint in a gene | Table 2, 2D |
| Gain 2E | 0 | The record contains the gain, a breakpoint in a gene | Table 2, 2E |
| Gain 2F | -1 | The gain contains the record and adds no gene | Table 2, 2F: "larger ..., does not include additional protein-coding genes" |
| Gain 2G | 0 | Any other overlap with a benign record | Table 2, 2G |

Section 3 counts the functional genes only. A CNV gets one benign-record row:
the record or records with the strongest criterion, in the order 2C, 2D, 2F,
2E, 2G, give it, and its `evidence_id` is `dosage:<ids>`. A gene-free gain
matches a record's gene content only inside it, as for 4O. The calculator
of the ClinGen CNV interface suggests -0.90 for gain 2F; XCNV uses the
published Table 2 default, -1.

### Criterion 4O

Criterion 4O is overlap with common population variation (Riggs et al. 2020,
Supplemental Material 1, categories 4L to 4O). `derive_cnv_2019_evidence()`
derives it from a `population` relation: one row per population record, with
its type (`loss` or `gain`) and the `frequency` that may support 4O.

| Rule | Source |
|---|---|
| The record has the CNV's type | Supplement: a common gain does not make a loss benign, and the reverse |
| The record holds the CNV's gene content: it contains the CNV's part of every functional gene that the CNV overlaps, or the whole CNV when it overlaps none | Supplement: the population CNV "includes the same gene content" |
| A gain that overlaps only part of a functional gene: no automatic 4O row | XCNV policy: BED intervals do not show the effect of a partial-gene gain on its transcripts (supplement, 2I to 2L), so such gains require manual evidence about breakpoints and transcripts |
| Frequency 1 % or more: -1 | Supplement: "common" is 1 % or more, default points |
| Frequency above 0.1 % and below 1 %: -0.90 | Supplement: less weight below 1 %; main text: such a CNV is a likely benign example. 0.1 % is the supplement's "relatively common" frequency (4N); -0.90 is the weight at which 4O alone is likely benign. This reading is XCNV's |
| Frequency 0.1 % or less: no row | as above |
| Frequency above 99 %: row shown, not selected | Supplement: such a frequency can be a reference artifact |
| A loss over a ClinGen autosomal recessive gene (dosage score 30): row shown, not selected | Supplement: carrier frequencies of recessive disease genes can exceed 1 % |
| A loss over an established haploinsufficient record: no row | Table 1: skip section 4 after such an overlap |

The record with the highest frequency gives the one row. Its `evidence_id` is
`population:<record>:<frequency>` and its `model_id` is
`4o-af0.01-0.001-gene-content`. The gnomAD-SV relation takes as `frequency`
the highest allele frequency of the continental groups with more than 2000
alleles (afr, amr, eas, nfe, sas), the population rule of the ClinGen CNV FAQ,
which applies the ClinGen SVI BA1 recommendation (Ghosh et al. 2018).

## The model

The published classifier is one tree with 41 nodes. XCNV stores it as a small
table and evaluates it in R. `tools/stage_xcnv_model.R` rebuilds this table from
the original XGBoost booster and checks both evaluators on 1,024 rows; only that
maintainer step needs XGBoost.
